description <- "
Panel C: ppk23 pheromone pathways produce opposite effects at different mAL subtypes
=====================================================================================
Top: Paired bar chart showing ppk23 (gold) and ppk25 (tan) net path strength
     per mAL subtype, ordered by ppk23 strength. ppk23 bars go NEGATIVE for
     F-selective subtypes, revealing the GABAergic sign inversion through AN05B035.

Bottom: Circuit diagram of two pathways:
  - Direct: ppk23 -> AN09B017a-e -> broad-contact mAL (positive)
  - Sign-inverted: ppk23 -> AN05B035 (GABA) -> AN09B017g -> F-selective mAL (negative)

Data: Path strength (exc - inh) through K strongest connectome paths.
"

## Extract ppk23 and ppk25 path strengths

```{r ppk-activations}
# Get ppk23 and ppk25 signed activation (exc - inh path strength) for each mAL subtype
ppk_data <- data.frame(
  target_type = mal_subtypes,
  ppk23 = mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, "ppk23"],
  ppk25 = mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, "ppk25"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Add annotations
ppk_data <- ppk_data %>%
  mutate(
    neurotransmitter = mal_nt[target_type]
  ) %>%
  arrange(ppk23)  # Order by ppk23 response

cat("ppk23 range:", range(ppk_data$ppk23), "\n")
cat("ppk25 range:", range(ppk_data$ppk25), "\n")
cat("Subtypes with negative ppk23:", sum(ppk_data$ppk23 < 0), "\n")
cat("Subtypes with positive ppk23:", sum(ppk_data$ppk23 > 0), "\n")
```

## Paired bar chart

```{r paired-bars, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
# Reshape for ggplot
ppk_long <- ppk_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ppk23, ppk25), names_to = "modality", values_to = "activation") %>%
  mutate(
    target_type = factor(target_type, levels = ppk_data$target_type),
    modality = factor(modality, levels = c("ppk23", "ppk25"))
  )

p_bars <- ggplot(ppk_long, aes(x = target_type, y = activation, fill = modality)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("ppk23" = "#FFD92F", "ppk25" = "#E5C494"),
    labels = c("ppk23", "ppk25")
  ) +
  labs(x = "mAL subtype", y = "Net path strength (exc − inh)",
       fill = "Sensory channel") +
  theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1, size = 6),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

save_fig5_plot(p_bars, "panel_C_ppk23_sign_reversal", width = 14, height = 6)
print(p_bars)
```

## Supplementary: GABA sign-inverter pool dual-channel sign inversion (ppk23 AND ppk25)

```{r dual-channel-supp, fig.width=11, fig.height=11}
# The GABA sign-inverter POOL (11 cells: AN05B021, AN05B023a-d, AN05B025,
# AN05B035, AN05B050_a, IN05B002, IN05B011a, IN05B011b) receives direct
# input from BOTH ppk23 AND ppk25 contact sensilla. The sign-inverted
# drive observed at F-selective mAL subtypes is therefore carried by
# BOTH channels, not only ppk23. This supplement makes that explicit
# by aggregating across the whole pool rather than singling out AN05B035.

stopifnot(exists("mal_paths"))

# Pool of GABA sign-inverter types (replicates setup_mspecific.R's
# gaba_sign_inverter_types definition; inlined here since panel_C sources
# setup.R only).
if (!exists("gaba_sign_inverter_types")) {
  .gaba_type_pool_c <- mba %>%
    dplyr::select(type, consensus_nt) %>%
    dplyr::distinct() %>%
    dplyr::group_by(type) %>% dplyr::slice(1) %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(consensus_nt), consensus_nt == "gaba",
                  grepl("^(AN05B|IN05)", type)) %>%
    dplyr::pull(type)
  .inh_interior_nodes_c <- mal_paths %>%
    dplyr::filter(valence == "inhibitory",
                  modality %in% c("ppk23","ppk25"),
                  end %in% mal_subtypes) %>%
    dplyr::pull(path) %>%
    lapply(function(p) {
      t <- strsplit(p, " -> ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      if (length(t) <= 2) character(0) else t[-c(1, length(t))]
    }) %>%
    unlist() %>% unique()
  gaba_sign_inverter_types <- intersect(.gaba_type_pool_c, .inh_interior_nodes_c)
  rm(.gaba_type_pool_c, .inh_interior_nodes_c)
}
cat("GABA sign-inverter pool (n =", length(gaba_sign_inverter_types), "):\n  ",
    paste(gaba_sign_inverter_types, collapse = ", "), "\n")

parse_path_nodes <- function(p) strsplit(p, " -> ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]

path_via_gaba_si_local <- function(path_str) {
  toks <- parse_path_nodes(path_str)
  if (length(toks) <= 2) return(FALSE)
  ints <- toks[-c(1, length(toks))]
  any(ints %in% gaba_sign_inverter_types)
}

compute_gaba_si_contribution <- function(modality_label) {
  # Per-mAL signed GABA sign-inverter pool contribution to <modality> drive.
  # Pick out <modality>-originated paths whose interior traverses any pool
  # member, sum strength, and negate (the pool is GABAergic -> sign-inverting).
  paths_mod <- mal_paths %>%
    filter(modality == modality_label, end %in% mal_subtypes)

  paths_mod <- paths_mod %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(via_pool = path_via_gaba_si_local(path)) %>%
    ungroup()

  via_df <- paths_mod %>%
    filter(via_pool) %>%
    group_by(end) %>%
    summarise(pool_raw = sum(strength, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  # Signed GABA SI pool contribution = negated raw path strength (GABA inversion)
  out <- data.frame(target_type = mal_subtypes, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(via_df, by = c("target_type" = "end")) %>%
    mutate(pool_raw = coalesce(pool_raw, 0),
           pool_signed = -pool_raw)
  out
}

gaba_ppk23 <- compute_gaba_si_contribution("ppk23") %>%
  rename(gaba_ppk23 = pool_signed) %>% select(target_type, gaba_ppk23)
gaba_ppk25 <- compute_gaba_si_contribution("ppk25") %>%
  rename(gaba_ppk25 = pool_signed) %>% select(target_type, gaba_ppk25)

dual_df <- data.frame(
  target_type = mal_subtypes,
  ppk23_drive = mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, "ppk23"],
  ppk25_drive = mal_activation_matrix[mal_subtypes, "ppk25"],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  left_join(gaba_ppk23, by = "target_type") %>%
  left_join(gaba_ppk25, by = "target_type") %>%
  arrange(ppk23_drive)

# Enforce shared x-axis ordering across all four panels
row_order <- dual_df$target_type
dual_df$target_type <- factor(dual_df$target_type, levels = row_order)

cat("GABA sign-inverter pool dual-channel contribution summary:\n")
cat(sprintf("  ppk23 signed contribution range: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            min(dual_df$gaba_ppk23), max(dual_df$gaba_ppk23)))
cat(sprintf("  ppk25 signed contribution range: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            min(dual_df$gaba_ppk25), max(dual_df$gaba_ppk25)))
cat(sprintf("  subtypes with nonzero GABA-SI-ppk23 contribution: %d/%d\n",
            sum(dual_df$gaba_ppk23 != 0), nrow(dual_df)))
cat(sprintf("  subtypes with nonzero GABA-SI-ppk25 contribution: %d/%d\n",
            sum(dual_df$gaba_ppk25 != 0), nrow(dual_df)))

# Shared colour convention:
#   Row 1 (ppk23 path drive)       -> red
#   Row 2 (ppk25 path drive)       -> orange
#   Row 3 (GABA SI pool -> ppk23)  -> dark blue (GABA / inversion)
#   Row 4 (GABA SI pool -> ppk25)  -> dark blue (GABA / inversion)
bar_fill_signed <- function(values, pos_col, neg_col) {
  ifelse(values >= 0, pos_col, neg_col)
}

plot_signed_bars <- function(values_col, pos_col, neg_col, y_lab) {
  df_i <- dual_df %>%
    mutate(val = .data[[values_col]],
           fill_col = bar_fill_signed(val, pos_col, neg_col))
  ggplot(df_i, aes(x = target_type, y = val, fill = fill_col)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, color = "black") +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_lab) +
    theme_pub(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 6),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )
}

# Unified Panel M palette:
#   ppk23 channel              -> red (pos) / muted red (neg)
#   ppk25 channel              -> orange (pos) / muted orange (neg)
#   GABA SI pool contribution  -> dark blue (inverting GABA)
#
# Mirror of setup_mspecific.R's canonical `panel_M_palette` (inlined here
# because panel_C sources setup.R only -- sourcing setup_mspecific.R would
# also run its male-specific mAL filter, which would shrink mal_subtypes
# used by the earlier chunks of this Rmd). Keep the hex codes in sync with
# figures/fig5/setup_mspecific.R:panel_M_palette.
if (!exists("panel_M_palette")) {
  panel_M_palette <- c(
    ppk23        = "#C0272D",  # red -- ppk23 contact-pheromone excitatory
    ppk25        = "#F4A261",  # orange -- ppk25 contact-pheromone excitatory
    gaba_si      = "#1F4E79"   # dark blue -- GABA sign-inverter pool
  )
}
stopifnot(all(c("ppk23", "ppk25", "gaba_si") %in% names(panel_M_palette)))

p1 <- plot_signed_bars("ppk23_drive",
                       pos_col = unname(panel_M_palette["ppk23"]),   # #C0272D
                       neg_col = "#7A1A1F",
                       y_lab = "ppk23 path drive\n(exc \u2212 inh)")
p2 <- plot_signed_bars("ppk25_drive",
                       pos_col = unname(panel_M_palette["ppk25"]),   # #F4A261
                       neg_col = "#B16A2D",
                       y_lab = "ppk25 path drive\n(exc \u2212 inh)")
p3 <- plot_signed_bars("gaba_ppk23",
                       pos_col = "#6790B8",
                       neg_col = unname(panel_M_palette["gaba_si"]), # #1F4E79
                       y_lab = "GABA sign-inverter signed\ncontrib. to ppk23 drive")
p4 <- plot_signed_bars("gaba_ppk25",
                       pos_col = "#6790B8",
                       neg_col = unname(panel_M_palette["gaba_si"]), # #1F4E79
                       y_lab = "GABA sign-inverter signed\ncontrib. to ppk25 drive")

# Strip x-axis labels from top 3 panels, keep bottom-most
p1 <- p1 + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
p2 <- p2 + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
p3 <- p3 + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
p4 <- p4 + labs(x = "mAL_m subtype (sorted by ppk23 path drive)")

p_dual <- p1 / p2 / p3 / p4 +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 1, 1.15)) +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "GABA sign-inverter pool inverts BOTH ppk23 and ppk25 contact-pheromone channels",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "Rows a-b: raw channel drives. Rows c-d: GABA sign-inverter pool routed component (n=%d pool members; dark blue where inhibitory).",
      length(gaba_sign_inverter_types)),
    tag_levels = "a",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, color = "grey25")
    )
  )

# Write straight to panel_M/pdf/ via panel_plot_dir("panel_M", "pdf")
pdf_dir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_M", "pdf")
png_dir <- panel_plot_dir("panel_M", "png")
ggsave(file.path(pdf_dir, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.pdf"),
       plot = p_dual, width = 11, height = 11)
ggsave(file.path(png_dir, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.png"),
       plot = p_dual, width = 11, height = 11, dpi = 300)
message(sprintf("  Wrote: %s", file.path(pdf_dir, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.pdf")))

# Mirror the Panel M dual-channel figure into plots_mspecific/ so that the
# male-specific Panel M directory stays in sync with this supplementary view.
pdf_dir_ms <- file.path(fig5_dir, "plots_mspecific", "panel_M", "pdf")
png_dir_ms <- file.path(fig5_dir, "plots_mspecific", "panel_M", "png")
dir.create(pdf_dir_ms, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(png_dir_ms, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(pdf_dir_ms, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.pdf"),
       plot = p_dual, width = 11, height = 11)
ggsave(file.path(png_dir_ms, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.png"),
       plot = p_dual, width = 11, height = 11, dpi = 300)
message(sprintf("  Wrote: %s", file.path(pdf_dir_ms, "panel_M_C_dual_channel.pdf")))

print(p_dual)
```

## Panel narrative

```{r narrative, echo=FALSE}
n_neg_ppk23 <- sum(ppk_data$ppk23 < 0)
n_pos_ppk23 <- sum(ppk_data$ppk23 > 0)
n_pos_ppk25 <- sum(ppk_data$ppk25 > 0)
most_neg <- ppk_data$target_type[which.min(ppk_data$ppk23)]
most_pos <- ppk_data$target_type[which.max(ppk_data$ppk23)]
ppk23_range <- range(ppk_data$ppk23)
ppk25_range <- range(ppk_data$ppk25)

neg_ppk23_types <- ppk_data %>% filter(ppk23 < 0) %>% pull(target_type)
pos_ppk23_types <- ppk_data %>% filter(ppk23 > 0) %>% pull(target_type)

n_neg_ppk25 <- sum(dual_df$gaba_ppk25 < 0)
n_neg_gaba_ppk23 <- sum(dual_df$gaba_ppk23 < 0)

narrative <- sprintf(
"PANEL C: Dual-Channel Sign Reversal at mAL via the GABA sign-inverter pool
==============================================================

WHAT THIS PANEL SHOWS
---------------------
Left: Paired bar chart showing ppk23 (gold) and ppk25 (tan) net path strength
for each mAL subtype, ordered by ppk23 response from most negative to most
positive. The zero line separates subtypes where ppk23 paths are net-inhibitory
(bars extending left/down) from those where ppk23 is net-excitatory.

Right: Scatter plot of ppk23 vs ppk25 net path strength, colored by
neurotransmitter. The quadrants separate subtypes by their response polarity
to each pheromone channel.

UPDATED FINDING (DUAL-CHANNEL GABA SIGN-INVERTER POOL INPUT)
------------------------------------------------------------
Contact-pheromone sign reversal is NOT carried by a single neuron: it is
distributed across an 11-cell GABA sign-inverter POOL (AN05B021, AN05B023a-d,
AN05B025, AN05B035, AN05B050_a, IN05B002, IN05B011a, IN05B011b). AN05B035 is
the highest-throughput member, but its siblings collectively carry a
comparable share of the inhibitory ppk23/ppk25 routing. Pool members receive
direct input from BOTH ppk23 and ppk25 contact sensilla; because the pool is
GABAergic, paths from EITHER channel that pass through any pool member are
sign-inverted before reaching their mAL_m targets.

The supplementary figure alongside this panel (panel_M/pdf/panel_M_C_dual_channel.pdf)
makes this explicit: row (a) ppk23 path drive, row (b) ppk25 path drive, row
(c) the GABA sign-inverter pool's signed contribution to ppk23 drive, row (d)
the same pool's signed contribution to ppk25 drive -- all sharing the same
mAL_m x-axis (sorted by ppk23 path drive). Rows (c) and (d) carry the same
negative-going signature, demonstrating that the pool's inhibitory imprint is
present on BOTH contact channels. Accordingly, sign reversal should be framed
as a property of the distributed GABA sign-inverter bottleneck, not as an
AN05B035-specific or ppk23-specific phenomenon.

KEY OBSERVATIONS
----------------
1. %d of %d mAL subtypes have NEGATIVE ppk23 net path strength, meaning
   ppk23 pheromone input is effectively inhibitory at these neurons.
   The most negative is %s (ppk23 = %.4f).

2. %d subtypes have positive ppk23, with %s being the strongest
   (ppk23 = %.4f).

3. ppk25 is positive in %d subtypes -- nearly all mAL neurons receive
   net-excitatory ppk25 pheromone input.

4. ppk23 ranges from %.4f to %.4f; ppk25 ranges from %.4f to %.4f.

5. Subtypes with negative ppk23 (%s) cluster in the
   negative-ppk23 / positive-ppk25 quadrant, while subtypes with positive
   ppk23 (%s) show positive responses to both channels.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
-------------------------
The ppk23 sign reversal is a circuit-level computation, not a receptor-level
property. ppk23 sensory neurons (WG4, LgLG1a, etc.) make excitatory synapses,
but a distributed pool of GABAergic ascending/interneurons (the GABA
sign-inverter pool: AN05B021, AN05B023a-d, AN05B025, AN05B035, AN05B050_a,
IN05B002, IN05B011a, IN05B011b) intercepts these signals and re-routes them
through an inhibitory relay to specific AN09B017 variants. Subtypes wired
through this inhibitory relay receive ppk23 as a net-negative signal.

This creates two functionally opposite mAL subpopulations:
  - ppk23-inhibited: excited by female (ppk25) but INHIBITED by male (ppk23)
    pheromones. These neurons could encode 'female-only' contact.
  - ppk23-excited: excited by both ppk23 and ppk25. These neurons could
    encode 'any conspecific contact' regardless of sex.

PLACE IN THE FIGURE 5 STORY
----------------------------
Panel C reveals the most surprising finding of the path analysis: the same
pheromone receptor (ppk23) produces opposite effects at different mAL subtypes.
This builds directly on Panel B's AN09B017 relay architecture (which showed
the GABA sign-inverter inhibitory branch) and provides the mechanistic basis
for the subtype diversity shown in Panel A. The sign reversal is further
decomposed into its excitatory and inhibitory components in Panel E.
",
n_neg_ppk23, nrow(ppk_data), most_neg, ppk23_range[1],
n_pos_ppk23, most_pos, ppk23_range[2],
n_pos_ppk25,
ppk23_range[1], ppk23_range[2], ppk25_range[1], ppk25_range[2],
paste(neg_ppk23_types, collapse = ", "),
paste(pos_ppk23_types, collapse = ", ")
)

save_panel_narrative("panel_C", narrative)
cat(narrative)
```
